pull.title: wallet: don't resubmit transactions under -privatebroadcast
pull.body:
This doesn't fix the general case of rebroadcasting potentially surprising users by divulging the originator IP trivially, but for users opting into private broadcast, it seems a bridge too far for them to expect the current behavior.

e.g. an incoming dust payment triggering your node to rebroadcast 24-36th later over clearnet

This can be removed if/when wallet drives through private broadcast.

see https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/3828 for running broader issue

> but for users opting into private broadcast, it seems a bridge too far for them to expect the current behavior.

Is it? The current behavior is that all transactions being sent via the wallet do not use private broadcast at all; `CommitTransaction` uses `MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_TO_ALL`, and it follows that resubmit behaves in the same way.

See also: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34533#issuecomment-3969991481

> The current behavior is that all transactions being sent via the wallet do not use private broadcast at all

This is true, but the case this change is protecting against is transactions sent by other means that also belong to the wallet.

So if a user is running with `-privatebroadcast` and is sending transactions via `sendrawtransaction`, if they have a watch only wallet or their addresses are dusted with low fee transactions, then the wallet will still rebroadcast these transactions. This could be unexpected if the user thinks they are protected by `-privatebroadcast`.

Is this intended for backport?

I ask because if we were not going to backport, then we could instead fix this by having the wallet use private broadcast. But for a backport fix this would be sufficient for existing users, with the tradeoff of reducing reliability of wallet transactions confirming a little bit.
@andrewtoth Given that wallet integration isn't close to done, I think we should remove footguns until we get there. This is easily reversed. I think backporting makes sense for the same reason.

events.body:
> I ask because if we were not going to backport, then we could instead fix this by having the wallet use private broadcast.

I think that promoting private broadcast into an essential feature (and with it, connectivity to privacy networks) that is required for basic functionality such as rebroadcasting is a major change that needs to be very well discussed, to say the least.

As of now I view it as an optional feature. 

But as such, I could see users starting with `-privatebroadcast` just to send out some transactions, and then restarting back to regular mode without private broadcast with a wallet that rebroadcasts them. This could reveal the origin of their transactions after the fact, so there is only so much this PR can achieve.

crACK https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/6d5450244b5539a454aee3f88152ef7c78e27055

It is unfortunate that restarting subjects a user to potentially losing privacy if a TX is not confirmed. I would personally be in favor of dropping wallet rebroadcasting completely, it is a massive privacy footgun for non-privatebroadcast users as well, for little benefit. At least, for little benefit that couldn't be provided with other solutions that are less harmful.

> I think that promoting private broadcast into an essential feature (and with it, connectivity to privacy networks) that is required for basic functionality such as rebroadcasting is a major change that needs to be very well discussed

I was merely suggesting to have the wallet rebroadcast via private broadcast if `-privatebroadcast` was set, not fix the entire unexpected rebroadcasting issue by requiring `-privatebroadcast`. (Although I might have shared that idea in another channel, I am not advocating we do that here.)

Improving privacy is good, but I think this has taken an odd approach:

* It adds a relationship between wallet behavior and `-privatebroadcast`. It is documented that `-privatebroadcast` does not affect the wallet.

* It makes it impossible to have `-privatebroadcast=1` and wallet rebroadcast. Wallet rebroadcast indeed looks bad wrt privacy, but it is so even without considering `-privatebroadcast`. There may be setups where the wallet rebroadcasts are not so bad (e.g. if the node is not directly connected to clearnet) and are desired. Wallet rebroadcasts shouldn't really be tied to the value of `-privatebroadcast`.

I think it is better to make wallet rebroadcasts separately controllable, independently of `-privatebroadcast`. Opened https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36380 to explore that.

events.message:
wallet: don't resubmit transactions to the mempool under -privatebroadcast

The wallet re-adds its unconfirmed transactions to the mempool periodically
and whenever a wallet is loaded or its transactions are imported. A
transaction that the rest of the network has dropped is then held by this
node alone, and served to any peer that asks for it, which marks it as the
node's own. Not announcing the re-added transaction does not hide this: any
relay peer can fetch anything in the mempool once the next inv round has
passed.

With -privatebroadcast, skip the resubmission entirely. Transactions sent
through the wallet are still submitted and announced as before, since those
never went through private broadcast in the first place.

events.body:
> Would be willing to discuss alternatives in an issue

One such alternative has an issue open https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/30471.

> @vasild I don't think adding more knobs is the right direction

Right, I am not convinced either. Maybe the existent option can be extended, see at the bottom of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36380#issuecomment-5906908312

> we already have `-walletbroadcast` which arguably could the a soft default with private broadcast on. Users could over-ride that and retain old behavior. But of course, users may turn the feature on, then turn it back off, rebroadcasting anyways.

I just don't like those parameter interactions - in general, they could be hard to reason about. So to have `-privatebroadcast=1` soft set `-walletbroadcast=0`? To stop also the initial wallet broadcast, given that `-privatebroadcast` is not used by the wallet... sounds odd to me.

> > It is documented that -privatebroadcast does not affect the wallet.
> 
> We can change documentation if we change behavior. Only matters if the change is correct/good/etc.

Right. And it would be nice to have the wallet use the private broadcast for its transactions even if currently it is documented that it does not :)

> the wallet rebroadcast feature ... is a massive leak

:100:
